te: So, what should you do if your cashless is denied at the counter tonight?
en: So, what should you do if your cashless is denied at the counter tonight?

te: Do not shout at hospital staff.
en: Do not shout at hospital staff.

te: Do not panic.
en: Do not panic.

te: Follow these four steps.
en: Follow these four steps.

te: Step One.
en: Step One.

te: Collect your papers before you leave.
en: Collect your papers before you leave.

te: If you have to pay the bill yourself, pay it.
en: If you have to pay the bill yourself, pay it.

te: But before leaving the hospital, ask for copies of the discharge summary, the final itemized bill, all test reports, pharmacy receipts, and the written cashless denial letter.
en: But before leaving the hospital, ask for copies of the discharge summary, the final itemized bill, all test reports, pharmacy receipts, and the written cashless denial letter.

te: If they claimed admission was not needed, ask your treating doctor for a short clinical justification certificate.
en: If they claimed admission was not needed, ask your treating doctor for a short clinical justification certificate.

te: Step Two.
en: Step Two.

te: File for reimbursement within fifteen to thirty days of discharge.
en: File for reimbursement within fifteen to thirty days of discharge.

te: Check your policy for your exact limit.
en: Check your policy for your exact limit.

te: If they reject it, write a calm, formal email to the company's Grievance Redressal Officer.
en: If they reject it, write a calm, formal email to the company's Grievance Redressal Officer.

te: State your policy number, claim number and amount, and if your policy has crossed five years, quote the I-R-D-A-I five-year moratorium rule.
en: State your policy number, claim number and amount, and if your policy has crossed five years, quote the I-R-D-A-I five-year moratorium rule.

te: The company must reply within fourteen days.
en: The company must reply within fourteen days.

te: Step Three.
en: Step Three.

te: Register on Bima Bharosa.
en: Register on Bima Bharosa.

te: If the company ignores you or sends the same generic rejection, go to Bima Bharosa dot I-R-D-A-I dot gov dot in.
en: If the company ignores you or sends the same generic rejection, go to Bima Bharosa dot I-R-D-A-I dot gov dot in.

te: This is the regulator's own portal, and complaints filed here are tracked directly by the I-R-D-A-I.
en: This is the regulator's own portal, and complaints filed here are tracked directly by the I-R-D-A-I.

te: And Step Four.
en: And Step Four.

te: The Insurance Ombudsman.
en: The Insurance Ombudsman.

te: If the company still refuses after thirty days, you do NOT need a consumer court case, and you do NOT need an expensive lawyer.
en: If the company still refuses after thirty days, you do NOT need a consumer court case, and you do NOT need an expensive lawyer.

te: Go to the official website, c-i-o-i-n-s dot co dot in.
en: Go to the official website, c-i-o-i-n-s dot co dot in.

te: The Insurance Ombudsman is a government body set up specifically to resolve insurance disputes.
en: The Insurance Ombudsman is a government body set up specifically to resolve insurance disputes.

te: You can file online.
en: You can file online.

te: It costs zero rupees.
en: It costs zero rupees.

te: You do not need a lawyer.
en: You do not need a lawyer.

te: In the financial year twenty twenty-four to twenty-five, the Ombudsman offices received over thirty-two thousand health complaints.
en: In the financial year twenty twenty-four to twenty-five, the Ombudsman offices received over thirty-two thousand health complaints.

te: Of the cases they settled or decided, over seventy-five percent went in favor of the policyholder.
en: Of the cases they settled or decided, over seventy-five percent went in favor of the policyholder.

te: And eight out of ten complaints were closed within three months.
en: And eight out of ten complaints were closed within three months.

te: The Ombudsman can award up to fifty lakh rupees, and the award is legally binding on the insurance company.
en: The Ombudsman can award up to fifty lakh rupees, and the award is legally binding on the insurance company.

te: Finally... how do you prevent this before you even buy?
en: Finally... how do you prevent this before you even buy?

te: Rule One.
en: Rule One.

te: Disclose everything in writing on the proposal form.
en: Disclose everything in writing on the proposal form.

te: If you smoke or take mild B-P medication, declare it.
en: If you smoke or take mild B-P medication, declare it.

te: Once it's on paper, they can never call it non-disclosure.
en: Once it's on paper, they can never call it non-disclosure.

te: Rule Two.
en: Rule Two.

te: Choose a policy with No Room Rent Capping.
en: Choose a policy with No Room Rent Capping.

te: In our example, one bigger room cost almost sixty thousand rupees through proportionate cuts.
en: In our example, one bigger room cost almost sixty thousand rupees through proportionate cuts.

te: Rule Three.
en: Rule Three.

te: Ask about a Consumables Cover.
en: Ask about a Consumables Cover.

te: Reports say gloves, masks, and syringes can be five to fifteen percent of a hospital bill.
en: Reports say gloves, masks, and syringes can be five to fifteen percent of a hospital bill.

te: Some insurers sell an add-on cover for this.
en: Some insurers sell an add-on cover for this.

te: Check its price and its limit before you buy.
en: Check its price and its limit before you buy.

te: Remember, you pay for insurance so your family has peace of mind.
en: Remember, you pay for insurance so your family has peace of mind.

te: Know the five-year rule.
en: Know the five-year rule.

te: Use the Ombudsman.
en: Use the Ombudsman.

te: And protect your hard-earned savings.
en: And protect your hard-earned savings.

te: Be smart.
en: Be smart.

te: Be informed.
en: Be informed.

te: And always... be practical.
en: And always... be practical.

te: If this helped you, share it with a family member who has health insurance, subscribe to Be Practical with Kishore, and ask your questions below.
en: If this helped you, share it with a family member who has health insurance, subscribe to Be Practical with Kishore, and ask your questions below.

te: I'll see you next time.
en: I'll see you next time.
